title: Apply the “Recurring issues should not” expectation when handling repeat problems
summary: When a problem appears to be a repeat, treat it as a “recurring issue” and use the expectation “Recurring issues should not… the same issues shouldn’t happen again and again” to guide what evidence you capture and to focus actions on preventing recurrence rather than only addressing the immediate symptom.
when_to_use: Use when you encounter a problem that has happened before and you need to decide whether it is truly the same issue and how to prevent it from repeating.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Apply the recurrence-prevention expectation; confirm whether the current incident matches the previously observed issue; decide whether available information is sufficient to identify what would prevent recurrence or whether to escalate.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to prior incident/problem information (ticket history or prior observations) as available in the site/support process

external_references: Prior incident/problem information (ticket history or prior observations) as available in the site/support process

visual_references.description: Training video frame containing the expectation statement: “Recurring issues should not… the same issues shouldn’t happen again and again…”.

steps.title: Treat the problem as a “recurring issue” when it has happened before
steps.purpose: Ensure you apply the recurrence-prevention expectation instead of handling the incident as a one-off symptom.
steps.instruction: When you encounter a problem that has happened before, explicitly treat it as a “recurring issue” rather than a one-off.
steps.expected_result: You have labeled the incident as a recurring issue (based on the fact it has happened before) and you are using that framing to guide your next evidence-gathering and troubleshooting focus.
steps.healthy_condition: The incident handling approach is oriented toward preventing the same issue from happening again and again.
steps.failure_condition: You treat the incident as a one-off and only address the immediate symptom without considering recurrence prevention.

actions.label: Classify as recurring
actions.exact_action: Explicitly treat it as a “recurring issue” rather than a one-off.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript: “Recurring issues should not… if we know that the same issues shouldn't happen again and again… does the support just.”

steps.title: Confirm the current incident is the “same issue” as the prior one
steps.purpose: Avoid applying recurrence-prevention actions to a different underlying problem that only looks similar.
steps.instruction: Compare what is happening now to what was previously reported/observed to confirm it is the same issue (not a different symptom).
steps.expected_result: You can state whether the current incident matches the previously observed issue (same issue vs different symptom).
steps.healthy_condition: The evidence you have supports that the current incident is the same issue that has occurred before.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm the issue is the “same issue” and you would otherwise assume recurrence-prevention applies.

actions.label: Compare current vs prior
actions.exact_action: Compare what is happening now to what was previously reported/observed to confirm it is the “same issue” (not a different symptom).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the issue cannot be confirmed as the “same issue,” do not assume recurrence-prevention applies to the current incident.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript near frame: “Recurring issues should not… the same issues shouldn't happen again and again…”

steps.title: Use the “Recurring issues should not” expectation to prevent recurrence
steps.purpose: Shift from symptom handling to recurrence prevention by focusing on underlying cause and what would stop the repeat.
steps.instruction: Use the expectation “Recurring issues should not” to guide your support actions toward preventing the repeat—focus on addressing the underlying cause rather than only the immediate occurrence.
steps.expected_result: Your troubleshooting/support actions are explicitly aimed at preventing the same issue from happening again and again (i.e., you are working toward identifying what would prevent recurrence).
steps.healthy_condition: Your evidence capture and next actions are oriented toward recurrence prevention rather than only resolving the current symptom.
steps.failure_condition: You only address the immediate occurrence and do not attempt to identify what would prevent recurrence.

actions.label: Orient actions to recurrence prevention
actions.exact_action: Focus on addressing the underlying cause rather than only the immediate occurrence.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript: “Recurring issues should not… if we know that the same issues shouldn't happen again and again…”

steps.title: Escalate if you cannot determine what would prevent recurrence
steps.purpose: Prevent the same issue from repeating when you lack sufficient information to identify recurrence-prevention actions.
steps.instruction: If you cannot identify what would prevent recurrence based on available information, stop and escalate for deeper troubleshooting rather than allowing the same issue to repeat.
steps.expected_result: You either (a) identify what would prevent recurrence, or (b) escalate because you cannot determine recurrence-prevention based on available information.
steps.healthy_condition: No recurrence-prevention guesswork is made when evidence is insufficient; escalation occurs when needed.
steps.failure_condition: You proceed without determining what would prevent recurrence, allowing the same issue to repeat.

actions.label: Escalate for deeper troubleshooting
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate for deeper troubleshooting rather than proceeding in a way that risks the same issue repeating.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot determine what would prevent recurrence, escalate rather than proceeding in a way that risks the same issue to repeat.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript frame includes the recurrence expectation: “Recurring issues should not… the same issues shouldn't happen again and again…”

success_criteria: The incident is treated as a recurring issue when it has happened before.
You confirm whether the current incident is the same issue as the prior one (not just a similar symptom).
Your actions are oriented toward preventing recurrence (identifying what would stop the repeat).
If recurrence-prevention cannot be determined from available information, you escalate rather than proceeding.
healthy_conditions: Recurrence-prevention framing is used for repeat problems.
Same-issue confirmation is performed before applying recurrence-prevention actions.
Escalation occurs when recurrence-prevention cannot be determined.
failure_conditions: Assuming recurrence-prevention applies when the issue cannot be confirmed as the same issue.
Proceeding without identifying what would prevent recurrence, allowing the same issue to repeat.
escalation_guidance: Escalate for deeper troubleshooting when you cannot determine what would prevent recurrence based on available information.
